raw:
"I remember being inside a cave when my flashlight went out. The entrance was around a bend, so I couldn’t see it from where I was. That was what frightened me—not just the light going out, but not being able to look back and see the way out.

There was cold water dripping onto my shoulders. I work as a swimming pool caretaker, so water itself is familiar, but it felt very different in there. Each drip drew my attention back to how cold and dark it was. I kept thinking about that bend and where the entrance was. With the flashlight working, I hadn’t thought so much about needing to see it. Once it went out, that was all I wanted—to see where I was going."
